reasoning derives or estimates the magnitude of accumulated numerical error for a proposed computation and relates that magnitude to the required tolerance in order to argue that the produced results will be accepted as equivalent.","parameters":[{"name":"reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text performing the error-magnitude estimate and the tolerance comparison."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning quantifies an expected error magnitude or bound for the proposed computation.","The reasoning explicitly relates that magnitude to the stated tolerance and concludes that the tolerance will or will not be met."],"exclusion_conditions":["The reasoning asserts correctness or equivalence without any error magnitude or bound.","The estimated quantity concerns something other than numerical accuracy (e.g. runtime or memory)."]},{"name":"PREDICTS_PERFORMANCE_FROM_COMPLEXITY_ESTIMATE","definition":"The reasoning estimates the cost or duration of competing implementations or commands from their operation counts, data sizes, or algorithmic complexity, and uses that estimate to support a performance judgement or an execution decision.","parameters":[{"name":"reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text containing the cost/complexity estimate and the conclusion drawn from it."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning gives a quantitative cost, operation-count, or duration estimate for at least one implementation or command.","The estimate is used to conclude that a performance requirement will be met, or to decide how the command should be executed (expected duration, timeout, background execution)."],"exclusion_conditions":["The reasoning names a performance requirement without estimating any cost or duration.","The estimate is purely about numerical accuracy rather than time or resource cost."]},{"name":"MIRRORS_REFERENCE_OPERATION_ORDER","definition":"The reasoning deliberately adopts the evaluation or accumulation order of a reference implementation described in the observation, so that the new implementation reproduces the reference's results within the required tolerance.","parameters":[{"name":"reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text stating that the new computation follows the reference implementation's order of operations in order to match its results."},{"name":"reference_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation containing the reference implementation or its computational procedure."}],"assertion_conditions":["The observation contains an implementation or computational procedure whose order of operations can be identified.","The reasoning explicitly states that the new computation reproduces that same order or sequence of operations, and links this choice to matching the reference results."],"exclusion_conditions":["The reasoning only states that results must match, without any reference to reproducing the reference's operation order.","The referenced content does not describe an implementation or computational procedure."]},{"name":"IMPLEMENTS_DECLARED_PLACEHOLDER_INTERFACE","definition":"A write action fills in the unfilled placeholder bodies of an artifact whose declared interface was observed earlier, supplying the missing implementation while preserving the declared names, signatures, and interface contract.","parameters":[{"name":"implementation_action","type":"action","description":"The write action producing the filled-in implementation."},{"name":"skeleton_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation showing the artifact with explicit unfilled placeholders and its declared interface elements."}],"assertion_conditions":["The observation shows an artifact containing explicit unfilled placeholders or stub bodies together with declared interface elements such as function names, argument order, or module name.","The action writes content that supplies those missing bodies while retaining the declared interface elements."],"exclusion_conditions":["The action creates a wholly new artifact for which no declared interface was observed.","The action only reads, inspects, or builds the artifact without supplying the missing bodies."]},{"name":"VERIFIES_EQUIVALENCE_AGAINST_REFERENCE","definition":"A comparison action evaluates both the candidate implementation and an independent reference implementation on identical inputs, and the observation reports quantified deviations that can be judged against a stated tolerance.","parameters":[{"name":"tolerance_reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text stating the required equivalence or tolerance that candidate results must meet."},{"name":"comparison_action","type":"action","description":"The action that runs the candidate and reference computations on the same inputs and computes their differences."},{"name":"deviation_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation reporting the quantified differences or explicit equality between candidate and reference outputs."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning states a tolerance or equivalence requirement for matching reference outputs.","The action evaluates candidate and reference results on identical inputs.","The observation reports quantified differences or explicit equality for the compared quantities."],"exclusion_conditions":["The action runs only the candidate implementation, with no reference computation in the same check.","The observation reports only an unquantified pass or fail without comparison to reference outputs."]},{"name":"EXECUTES_LONG_RUNNING_COMMAND_ASYNCHRONOUSLY","definition":"The reasoning anticipates that a command will run for a long time relative to interactive waiting, and the corresponding action is dispatched in a non-blocking manner so that other work can continue.","parameters":[{"name":"cost_reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text anticipating the long duration of the command."},{"name":"dispatch_action","type":"action","description":"The action that launches the long-running command asynchronously or with an extended timeout."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning states or implies that the command's runtime is long relative to interactive waiting.","The action is launched in a non-blocking or asynchronous mode, or with an explicitly extended timeout."],"exclusion_conditions":["The action runs synchronously despite an anticipated long runtime.","No runtime expectation is expressed before the command is launched."]},{"name":"STAGES_CHEAP_PROBE_BEFORE_COSTLY_VALIDATION","definition":"The reasoning orders verification into two tiers, deciding that a fast low-cost check on a small or reduced case is executed first, and that the expensive full-scale validation is deferred until after that probe.","parameters":[{"name":"sequencing_reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text expressing the intent to run a quick reduced check before the full or expensive validation."},{"name":"precursor_check_action","type":"action","description":"The action executing the reduced or small-scale check."},{"name":"full_validation_action","type":"action","description":"The action executing the complete, expensive, required workload after the precursor check."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning expresses the intent to perform a quick check before the full or expensive validation.","The precursor action exercises a reduced or small-scale case.","The full validation action exercises the complete required workload and occurs after the precursor action."],"exclusion_conditions":["Only one of the two verification steps is performed.","The first action already exercises the full workload rather than a reduced case."]},{"name":"BROADENS_VERIFICATION_BEYOND_REQUIRED_CASES","definition":"The reasoning identifies additional input conditions or variations that the stated requirements and given test harness do not exercise, and plans to verify them in order to reduce the risk of undetected failure.","parameters":[{"name":"reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The agent text naming extra input variations and stating the intention to test them."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning names at least one input variation not exercised by the stated test harness, such as a size edge case, alternative memory layout, alternative data type, or malformed input.","The reasoning states that these extra checks will be performed to gain additional assurance beyond the required tests."],"exclusion_conditions":["The reasoning only repeats the tests required by the task specification.","Additional checks are mentioned without identifying any concrete input variation to be exercised."]}],"uncertain":[]}

new.name: JUSTIFIES_NUMERICAL_EQUIVALENCE_BY_ERROR_ANALYSIS
new.definition: The reasoning derives or estimates the magnitude of accumulated numerical error for a proposed computation and relates that magnitude to the required tolerance in order to argue that the produced results will be accepted as equivalent.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text performing the error-magnitude estimate and the tolerance comparison.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning quantifies an expected error magnitude or bound for the proposed computation.
The reasoning explicitly relates that magnitude to the stated tolerance and concludes that the tolerance will or will not be met.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning asserts correctness or equivalence without any error magnitude or bound.
The estimated quantity concerns something other than numerical accuracy (e.g. runtime or memory).

new.name: PREDICTS_PERFORMANCE_FROM_COMPLEXITY_ESTIMATE
new.definition: The reasoning estimates the cost or duration of competing implementations or commands from their operation counts, data sizes, or algorithmic complexity, and uses that estimate to support a performance judgement or an execution decision.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text containing the cost/complexity estimate and the conclusion drawn from it.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning gives a quantitative cost, operation-count, or duration estimate for at least one implementation or command.
The estimate is used to conclude that a performance requirement will be met, or to decide how the command should be executed (expected duration, timeout, background execution).
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning names a performance requirement without estimating any cost or duration.
The estimate is purely about numerical accuracy rather than time or resource cost.

new.name: MIRRORS_REFERENCE_OPERATION_ORDER
new.definition: The reasoning deliberately adopts the evaluation or accumulation order of a reference implementation described in the observation, so that the new implementation reproduces the reference's results within the required tolerance.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text stating that the new computation follows the reference implementation's order of operations in order to match its results.

parameters.name: reference_observation
parameters.description: The observation containing the reference implementation or its computational procedure.

assertion_conditions: The observation contains an implementation or computational procedure whose order of operations can be identified.
The reasoning explicitly states that the new computation reproduces that same order or sequence of operations, and links this choice to matching the reference results.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only states that results must match, without any reference to reproducing the reference's operation order.
The referenced content does not describe an implementation or computational procedure.

new.name: IMPLEMENTS_DECLARED_PLACEHOLDER_INTERFACE
new.definition: A write action fills in the unfilled placeholder bodies of an artifact whose declared interface was observed earlier, supplying the missing implementation while preserving the declared names, signatures, and interface contract.

parameters.name: implementation_action
parameters.description: The write action producing the filled-in implementation.

parameters.name: skeleton_observation
parameters.description: The observation showing the artifact with explicit unfilled placeholders and its declared interface elements.

assertion_conditions: The observation shows an artifact containing explicit unfilled placeholders or stub bodies together with declared interface elements such as function names, argument order, or module name.
The action writes content that supplies those missing bodies while retaining the declared interface elements.
exclusion_conditions: The action creates a wholly new artifact for which no declared interface was observed.
The action only reads, inspects, or builds the artifact without supplying the missing bodies.

new.name: VERIFIES_EQUIVALENCE_AGAINST_REFERENCE
new.definition: A comparison action evaluates both the candidate implementation and an independent reference implementation on identical inputs, and the observation reports quantified deviations that can be judged against a stated tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text stating the required equivalence or tolerance that candidate results must meet.

parameters.name: comparison_action
parameters.description: The action that runs the candidate and reference computations on the same inputs and computes their differences.

parameters.name: deviation_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the quantified differences or explicit equality between candidate and reference outputs.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states a tolerance or equivalence requirement for matching reference outputs.
The action evaluates candidate and reference results on identical inputs.
The observation reports quantified differences or explicit equality for the compared quantities.
exclusion_conditions: The action runs only the candidate implementation, with no reference computation in the same check.
The observation reports only an unquantified pass or fail without comparison to reference outputs.

new.name: EXECUTES_LONG_RUNNING_COMMAND_ASYNCHRONOUSLY
new.definition: The reasoning anticipates that a command will run for a long time relative to interactive waiting, and the corresponding action is dispatched in a non-blocking manner so that other work can continue.

parameters.name: cost_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text anticipating the long duration of the command.

parameters.name: dispatch_action
parameters.description: The action that launches the long-running command asynchronously or with an extended timeout.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states or implies that the command's runtime is long relative to interactive waiting.
The action is launched in a non-blocking or asynchronous mode, or with an explicitly extended timeout.
exclusion_conditions: The action runs synchronously despite an anticipated long runtime.
No runtime expectation is expressed before the command is launched.

new.name: STAGES_CHEAP_PROBE_BEFORE_COSTLY_VALIDATION
new.definition: The reasoning orders verification into two tiers, deciding that a fast low-cost check on a small or reduced case is executed first, and that the expensive full-scale validation is deferred until after that probe.

parameters.name: sequencing_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text expressing the intent to run a quick reduced check before the full or expensive validation.

parameters.name: precursor_check_action
parameters.description: The action executing the reduced or small-scale check.

parameters.name: full_validation_action
parameters.description: The action executing the complete, expensive, required workload after the precursor check.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning expresses the intent to perform a quick check before the full or expensive validation.
The precursor action exercises a reduced or small-scale case.
The full validation action exercises the complete required workload and occurs after the precursor action.
exclusion_conditions: Only one of the two verification steps is performed.
The first action already exercises the full workload rather than a reduced case.

new.name: BROADENS_VERIFICATION_BEYOND_REQUIRED_CASES
new.definition: The reasoning identifies additional input conditions or variations that the stated requirements and given test harness do not exercise, and plans to verify them in order to reduce the risk of undetected failure.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text naming extra input variations and stating the intention to test them.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning names at least one input variation not exercised by the stated test harness, such as a size edge case, alternative memory layout, alternative data type, or malformed input.
The reasoning states that these extra checks will be performed to gain additional assurance beyond the required tests.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only repeats the tests required by the task specification.
Additional checks are mentioned without identifying any concrete input variation to be exercised.
